selected_evidence.requirement: opsadmin user created with the specified SSH public key installed
selected_evidence.summary: opsadmin user created, ~/.ssh created (700), public key written to authorized_keys (600, owned by opsadmin), key content verified to match exactly

selected_evidence.requirement: SSH restricted to key-based authentication only
selected_evidence.summary: sshd_config.d drop-in enforcing PasswordAuthentication no / PubkeyAuthentication yes validated with sshd -t, sshd reloaded, effective config confirmed via sshd -T, sshd listener confirmed active on :22

selected_evidence.requirement: Live proof key-only auth is enforced (pre-restart)
selected_evidence.summary: ssh with PreferredAuthentications=password immediately returns 'Permission denied (publickey)' with no password prompt, proving password auth is disabled
Captured boot_id ad55b012-ab66-4384-974c-3ffd0c32a7d0, uptime -s, sshd status started, opsadmin passwd entry, and authorized_keys permissions before reboot
Backgrounded 'sudo reboot' returned its ack (pid) before the connection dropped; subsequent poll immediately failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down

selected_evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving an actual restart occurred
selected_evidence.summary: After polling through the outage, node1 responded with boot_id 69b3f677-49c3-4466-a87f-63bbbf8c5c11 (different from baseline ad55b012...) and a fresh uptime -s timestamp

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of opsadmin/key-only SSH configuration
selected_evidence.summary: After restart: sshd running, effective config still key-only (pubkey yes / password no / kbdinteractive no / permitemptypasswords no), opsadmin user and authorized_keys intact with correct permissions, password still locked, and live password-auth attempt still rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)'
